audit_scope.include: Published tasks that use auditory and tactile stimuli to estimate or probe peripersonal-space related audio-tactile integration.
audit_scope.exclude: Clinical population labels, intervention labels, social/mannequin/VR/locomotion context, and extra non-audiotactile manipulations are not blockers unless they change the auditory stimulus, tactile stimulus, response, timing, trial design, spatial geometry, or apparatus used by the PPS task.
audit_scope.profile_check_goal: Decide whether the audiotactile PPS task can be represented as a standardized PPS Toolkit profile, not whether every original clinical or contextual manipulation is reproduced. The acceptance gate focuses on stimulus type/assets, ITI or jitter, SOAs, baseline strategy, and trial repetition count; routine randomization and block order are reproducible implementation defaults rather than blockers. Two-speaker analog setups are treated as apparatus provenance: when papers report enough trajectory/timing/source parameters, their motion is recreated with the toolkit binaural renderer rather than treated as a distinct audio source.

blocker_definition.analog_speaker_reconstruction_policy: Original two-speaker looming/receding setups are not structural blockers by themselves. The profile should extract the reported near/far distances, trajectory/duration, SOAs, baseline, and repetitions, then recreate the moving sound with the binaural spatial renderer. Exact original gain/envelope files remain missing-publication provenance only when exact author-stimulus equivalence is required.

standardization_gap_groups.label: Spatial coordinate system

standardization_gap_groups.label: Tactile and response mapping
standardization_gap_groups.question: Can the profile represent tactile modality, site, channel, duration, calibration, response modality, and response rule rather than assuming simple button detection?

standardization_gap_groups.label: Timing and repetition

standardization_gap_groups.label: External trigger contract
standardization_gap_groups.question: If physiology is part of the task execution, can the profile preserve the required event triggers and timing without treating the clinical or neurophysiology endpoint itself as a blocker?

constraint_taxonomy.description: Static near/far auditory positions paired with tactile targets are supported through stationary source rows in generated Segment 5/6 blocks; paper-specific profiles still need exact distances, timing, response mapping, and apparatus parameters.

Go/NoGo tactile target logic with weak target rows, strong/non-target tactile rows, sound-only/no-target catches, and explicit respond-vs-withhold scoring. The runner now supports this as row-level Expected_Response/Target_Role metadata; paper-specific voice-key, electrical calibration, timing, and profile-translation parameters can still block individual studies.
Tactile discrimination or localization responses rather than simple speeded detection.
Auditory-tactile extinction or neglect-style response mapping rather than speeded tactile detection.
The PPS readout combines auditory, visual, and tactile stimuli in the same task family, so an exact profile needs more than audio-tactile stimulus fields.
Tactile-only baseline trials whose timing is coupled to specific sound-motion endpoints such as T0/T6.
Core PPS-task values such as trial repetition counts, ITIs, SOAs, distance/timing tables, or baseline timing are not reported or not encoded. Ordinary randomization and block order are not blockers.
Profiles requiring explicit expectancy or hazard-rate control across fixed, flat, dynamic, near, far, and baseline trials.

Physical multi-speaker arrays can be represented when the paper reports a single serial trajectory with distances and timing that map onto the toolkit moving-source renderer; true front/back or concurrently switched arrays still need explicit source-switching support.
Speaker-array Gaussian amplitude fields; reducible serial trajectories can be represented as virtual moving-source paths when source papers report enough timing and distance anchors.
Study-specific HRTF or binaural rendering resource differs from the bundled toolkit renderer.
Unity/3D Tune-In runtime behavior is part of the auditory stimulus definition.
Distances are expressed in subject-scaled units such as arm length rather than absolute cm/m.
Spatial coordinates are anchored to hand, trunk, head, lateral hemispace, or a body-landmark frame not represented as a first-class profile coordinate system.

Rear-left and rear-right trajectories are distinct task families rather than one mirrored direction parameter. Current preload assets can expand them when the paper reports enough coordinates and timings; otherwise rear/front body-relative mapping remains a structural blocker.
Ecological, affective, animal, music, voice, or proprietary sounds are required and not redistributable or not exactly identified.
Exact amplitude envelope, SoundForge gain file, or rendered source file is part of the task and is missing.
Original response was vocal/voice-key rather than mouse/button timing.
Electrical tactile stimulation requires pulse parameters and participant threshold calibration.
The tactile stimulus is defined by a waveform/frequency profile, such as an 80 Hz sawtooth vibration, rather than only by site, channel, and duration.

The PPS stimulus schedule requires an explicit event-trigger or synchronization contract for TMS/MEP, iEEG, fMRI, EEG, or sleep/consciousness recording; the physiology endpoint itself is context, not a blocker.

current_template_coverage.source_notes: GUI-recreatable with reported 216-trial PPS-assessment formula; physical Gaussian speaker arrays are represented as front/back virtual moving-source trajectories.

GUI-recreatable with twelve published 3D source directions, dynamic moving pink-noise and flat stationary pink-noise source families, six arm-length-scaled tactile timepoints represented using a declared 70 cm reference arm length, and 144 preview trial rows; exact Unity/3D Tune-In rendering and per-subject body/head scaling remain recreation caveats.

Profile now expands both reported rear hemispaces into four source assets: dog/sheep x rear-left/rear-right. Publisher HTML methods review on 2026-07-15 confirmed 3000 ms sounds, 520-to-20 cm rear trajectories at -135 and +135 degrees, Tbefore/T1-T5/Tafter tactile timings, 224 tactile-target trials, 32 auditory-only catches, and eight 32-trial blocks. The profile remains blocked because the exact dog/sheep source audio, Audacity matching settings, LISTEN HRTF subject/filter choice, and renderer settings are not available in the public toolkit.
